title: Panorra API Go Get Project Report

issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/08/26

✅ Implementation: Detail Post V2 API

Summary

Added a V2 detail-post endpoint. Published posts retain the filtering behavior of views_timeline_post; processing posts use a restricted owner-only query with published fallback.

Route

GET /v2/posts/:slug

Registered through src/Routes/V2/PostsRoutes.go:

func PostRoutes(router fiber.Router) {
    posts := router.Group("/posts")
    posts.Get("/:slug", Controllers.DetailPost)
}

The V2 route group is registered in src/Routes/V1/Routes.go:

V2 := http.Group("v2")
V2Routes.PostRoutes(V2)

Access and Filtering

  • Roles user and viewer are accepted.
  • Published posts are selected from views_timeline_post.
  • The view enforces published posts, non-banned posts, and non-banned owners.
  • Redis-backed blocked-post, blocked-user, and deactivated-user exclusions follow Detail Post V1 behavior.
  • Private posts are available only to their owner.
  • isprocessing=true selects only the authenticated user's processing, unpublished, non-banned post.
  • If no processing post is found, the action falls back to the published view.

Response Structure

The action returns the requested post fields and groups related data:

{
  "description": {
    "full": "...",
    "short": "...",
    "long": "..."
  },
  "user": {
    "username": "...",
    "avatar": "...",
    "fullname": "..."
  }
}

For authenticated users, direct queries resolve:

  • liked from like.
  • bookmark from bookmark.
  • folder_slug from folder_bookmark.

For viewers, these values remain false, false, and null.

Description Truncation

Updated PostFunctions.WrapText to keep its existing limits:

  • short: 250 Unicode runes.
  • long: 500 Unicode runes.
  • full: unescaped source description without truncation.

The truncation helper treats these patterns as atomic tokens:

@[username](encrypt)
#[hashtag]()

When a limit occurs inside either token, output ends before the token instead of returning malformed markup.

Tests cover mention truncation, hashtag truncation, complete tokens below the limit, and multibyte Unicode limits.

Database View

Added migrations/20260807_update_views_timeline_post_v2.sql and updated the reference DDL.

The migration preserves the order and names of all existing columns required by PostgreSQL CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW. New columns are appended after hotspot:

posts.id,
categories.name AS category_name,
posts.location_group,
posts.location_group_slug

It adds:

LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.categories ON categories.id = posts.category_id

Existing view filters remain unchanged:

posts.is_publish = true
AND posts.banned = false
AND users.banned = false

Files Changed

  • src/Action/V2/Posts/DetailPost.go
  • src/Controllers/V2/PostsController.go
  • src/Routes/V2/PostsRoutes.go
  • src/Routes/V1/Routes.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/PostsFunctions.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/PostsFunctions_test.go
  • migrations/20260807_update_views_timeline_post_v2.sql
  • docs/migrations/views/DDL_views_timeline_post.sql

Verification

Ran:

go test ./src/Action/V2/Posts ./src/Controllers/V2 ./src/Routes/V2 ./src/Routes/V1 ./src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions

Result: pass. Description truncation tests pass; other listed packages contain no test files.

Objective

Add a V2 detail-post API with structured description variants, location metadata, post-owner data, and authenticated-user interaction status.

Route

GET /v2/posts/:slug

Optional processing query:

GET /v2/posts/:slug?isprocessing=true

Requirements

  • Allow roles user and viewer.
  • Use views_timeline_post as the source for published posts so its published, post-ban, and owner-ban filters remain authoritative.
  • For isprocessing=true, first look for the authenticated user's unpublished processing post, then fall back to the published view.
  • Preserve Detail Post V1 rules for blocked posts, blocked users, deactivated users, and private visibility.
  • Return slug, animation, animation_filter, little_planet, little_planet_filter, category_name, created_at, location fields, panorama fields, thumbnail, potd, and visibility.
  • Return owner data under user with username, avatar, and fullname.
  • Return description under description.full, description.short, and description.long.
  • Limit description.short to 250 Unicode characters and description.long to 500 Unicode characters.
  • Never split mention tokens (@[username](encrypt)) or hashtag tokens (#[hashtag]()) during description truncation. If a limit falls inside a token, truncate before that token.
  • For role user, resolve liked, bookmark, and folder_slug from authenticated-user data.
  • For role viewer, return liked=false, bookmark=false, and folder_slug=null.
  • Preserve the existing encrypted-response behavior when header ec=true.
  • Update views_timeline_post without dropping it. Preserve all existing view-column positions and append new columns only at the end.

Response

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 2,
    "messages": "Detail Post",
    "post": {
      "slug": "post-slug",
      "animation": false,
      "animation_filter": {},
      "little_planet": false,
      "little_planet_filter": {},
      "description": {
        "full": "Full description",
        "short": "Description up to 250 characters",
        "long": "Description up to 500 characters"
      },
      "category_name": "Travel",
      "created_at": "2026-08-07T00:00:00Z",
      "location_name": "Bangkok",
      "location_post": {},
      "location_group": "Bangkok",
      "location_group_slug": "bangkok",
      "panorama": "panorama.jpg",
      "panorama_preview": "preview.jpg",
      "panorama_quality": {},
      "thumbnail": "thumbnail.jpg",
      "bookmark": false,
      "folder_slug": null,
      "liked": false,
      "potd": false,
      "user": {
        "username": "username",
        "avatar": "avatar.jpg",
        "fullname": "Full Name"
      },
      "visibility": "public"
    }
  }
}

View Migration

Append these columns to views_timeline_post after every existing column:

posts.id,
categories.name AS category_name,
posts.location_group,
posts.location_group_slug

Add the category join:

LEFT JOIN panorra_dev.public.categories ON categories.id = posts.category_id

Keep the existing filters:

posts.is_publish = true
AND posts.banned = false
AND users.banned = false

Files

  • src/Action/V2/Posts/DetailPost.go
  • src/Controllers/V2/PostsController.go
  • src/Routes/V2/PostsRoutes.go
  • src/Routes/V1/Routes.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/PostsFunctions.go
  • src/Utils/Functions/PostFunctions/PostsFunctions_test.go

issues.display_title: Issue #495: Post Aggregate Bookmark and Share Counters
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/08/26

✅ Implementation: Post Aggregate Bookmark and Share Counters

Summary

Extended /posts/agg/:sid to return bookmark and share counters from Elasticsearch. Older post documents remain compatible because missing new fields resolve to zero.

Counter Types

The accepted type values are now:

like
comment
view
bookmark
share

Elasticsearch field mapping:

like      -> counter_like
comment   -> counter_comment
view      -> counter_view
bookmark  -> counter_bookmark
share     -> counter_share

Default Counters

Added a common zero-value document:

func defaultPostCounters() map[string]interface{} {
    return map[string]interface{}{
        "counter_comment":  0,
        "counter_like":     0,
        "counter_view":     0,
        "counter_share":    0,
        "counter_bookmark": 0,
    }
}

This default is used when the Elasticsearch post document has no counter data.

Missing Field Compatibility

Added postCounter to resolve counter_<type> safely. It returns zero when:

  • The requested field does not exist.
  • The stored value has an unsupported type.
  • An older Elasticsearch document only has comment, like, and view counters.

The helper supports Elasticsearch float64 values and integer defaults.

Response Handling

like remains separate because it also checks and returns liked.

The counter-only types share one branch:

case "comment", "view", "bookmark", "share":
    counter = postCounter(postCounts, tyepeCounter)
    res["counter"] = counter

No existing access, visibility, blocking, or encryption behavior changed.

Tests

Added tests for:

  • Missing bookmark and share fields returning zero.
  • Existing Elasticsearch float64 counter values.
  • Integer values in the default counter document.
  • All five default counters returning zero.

API Collection

Updated Post Aggregate.yml:

  • Counter-type description now includes bookmark and share.
  • Added a Bookmark response example.
  • Added a Share response example.

Files Changed

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostAgg.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostAgg_test.go
  • api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/Posts/Post Aggregate.yml

Verification

Ran:

go test ./src/Action/V1/Posts ./src/Controllers/V1 ./src/Routes/V1

Result: pass.

Objective

Extend the Post Aggregate API with bookmark and share counters while keeping compatibility with older Elasticsearch post documents that do not contain the new counter properties.

Route

GET /posts/agg/:sid?type=:counter_type

Requirements

  • Preserve existing like, comment, and view counter behavior.
  • Accept two new counter types:
    • bookmark, mapped to counter_bookmark.
    • share, mapped to counter_share.
  • Return missing counter_bookmark and counter_share values as 0 for older Elasticsearch documents.
  • When the Elasticsearch document is empty, initialize all post counters with zero:
map[string]interface{}{
    "counter_comment":  0,
    "counter_like":     0,
    "counter_view":     0,
    "counter_share":    0,
    "counter_bookmark": 0,
}
  • Handle Elasticsearch numeric values and integer default values without unsafe type assertions.
  • Keep like handling separate because its response also contains liked.
  • Share one switch branch for comment, view, bookmark, and share because all four only return counter.
  • Preserve role validation, blocked-post checks, deactivated-user filtering, private-post filtering, and encrypted responses.
  • Update the existing Post Aggregate API collection with bookmark and share examples.

Response

Bookmark example:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "counter": 0
  }
}

Share example:

{
  "statusCode": 200,
  "data": {
    "valid": true,
    "version": 0,
    "counter": 0
  }
}

Files

  • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostAgg.go
  • src/Action/V1/Posts/PostAgg_test.go
  • api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/Posts/Post Aggregate.yml

Verification

go test ./src/Action/V1/Posts ./src/Controllers/V1 ./src/Routes/V1

issues.display_title: Issue #489: API: Support 360 vertical post detail flow
issues.main_description_html:
API: Support 360 Vertical Post Detail Flow

Context

UI task GoThruMedia/panorra#2834 defines a TikTok-like vertical 360 photo post detail experience for Panorra Mobile.

The API repo already has post detail and interaction endpoints such as:

  • GET /posts/detail?slug=<slug>
  • GET /posts/sl/detail/:sid
  • GET /posts/sl/agg/:sid
  • comment list endpoints under /comments
  • like/check-like endpoints under /posts and /users

This task should confirm and extend the API contract needed by the vertical 360 post detail UI.

Scope

Support API data for:

  • Single 360 photo post detail
  • Carousel/multiple 360 photo post detail
  • Right action bar state: like, comment count, save/bookmark, share
  • Bottom overlay data: category, place title, description, rating/distance/views where available
  • Comment bottom sheet
  • Share link metadata
  • Ellipsis menu actions

Proposed Endpoint Strategy

Prefer extending existing post detail APIs instead of creating a duplicate detail endpoint.

Primary detail endpoint:

GET /posts/sl/detail/:sid?sl=true&include=<fields>

or an existing compatible equivalent.

Optional new vertical feed endpoint if the mobile app needs swipe-to-next/previous post context:

GET /posts/sl/vertical-detail-feed

Query params:

slug=<current_post_slug>
source=home|place|profile|search|share
lat=<float>
lng=<float>
page=<int>
limit=<int>
category_id=<int>
include=<comma-separated-fields>

Response Requirements

The post detail response should support:

  • id where allowed
  • slug
  • post_type
  • category_id
  • category_name
  • created_at
  • description
  • short_description
  • long_description
  • location_name
  • location_post
  • panorama
  • panorama_preview
  • thumbnail
  • panorama_quality
  • animation
  • animation_filter
  • little_planet
  • little_planet_filter
  • multiple_posts for carousel/multiple 360 posts
  • views_aggregate
  • likes_aggregate
  • comments_aggregate
  • bookmark
  • folder_id
  • folder
  • liked or equivalent check-like state
  • user
  • visibility
  • potd
  • pending
  • share_url

Carousel / Multiple 360 Requirements

For carousel posts, API should return ordered media/viewpoints:

"multiple_posts": [
  {
    "thumbnail": "...",
    "panorama": "...",
    "panorama_preview": "...",
    "panorama_quality": {},
    "location_name": "...",
    "location_post": {},
    "sequence": 1
  }
]

Requirements:

  • Preserve sequence order.
  • Include enough fields for thumbnail preview and 360 viewer loading.
  • Support single-post and carousel response shapes without forcing the UI into extra waterfall calls.

Comment Requirements

Confirm existing comment APIs support the bottom sheet:

  • list comments for a post
  • list replies
  • previous pagination
  • comment like state/count
  • total comment count

If missing, add support for:

  • cursor/page pagination
  • authenticated user liked-comment state
  • reply count per comment
  • stable sort by newest or relevant default

Action State Requirements

For authenticated users:

  • Return whether current user liked the post.
  • Return whether current user saved/bookmarked the post.
  • Return bookmark folder info when available.
  • Respect blocked post/user and private visibility behavior.

For viewers/guests:

  • Return safe public detail data.
  • Do not expose private/blocked content.
  • Return action states as false/null where auth is required.

Share Requirements

Add or confirm share metadata response:

  • canonical share_url
  • title/place name
  • thumbnail
  • post slug
  • post type

Acceptance Criteria

  • Mobile can load a single 360 post detail with all fields needed by the vertical viewer.
  • Mobile can load carousel/multiple 360 post detail without unnecessary extra waterfall calls.
  • API returns action bar state: like count/state, comment count, bookmark state, views.
  • Comment bottom sheet can be populated from existing or extended comment APIs.
  • Share sheet has canonical share URL and metadata.
  • Private, blocked, deactivated, pending, and missing posts return correct errors.
  • Existing post detail clients remain backward compatible.
  • API collection is updated with examples for single and carousel 360 post detail.

Related

  • UI task: GoThruMedia/panorra#2834
  • Possibly related older API task: #360

issues.display_title: Issue #486: API: Support Home Places Near You with category filtering
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 07/08/26

✅ Implementation: Home Places Near You Category Filtering

Summary

Extended GET /places/list for Panorra Mobile Home "Places Near You" preview, expanded list, category filtering, map synchronization, nearby search, sorting, radius filtering, and pagination.

Route

GET /places/list

Supported query parameters:

lat=<float>
lng=<float>
radius=<km>
category_id=<int>
search=<string>
sort=best_match|nearest|most_popular|most_posts|recently_added
page=<int>
limit=<int>
include=<comma-separated-fields>
mode=preview|expanded

Category Filtering

category_id is optional.

  • Without category_id, the endpoint returns nearby places across all categories.
  • With category_id, only posts from that category contribute to places, totals, thumbnails, contributors, markers, and pagination.
  • Category IDs are checked against the categories table.
  • Invalid or unknown category IDs return 400.
  • A valid category without matching places returns 200 with an empty data_places array.

Each place response now includes:

{
  "category_id": 1,
  "category_name": "Nature"
}

Without a category filter, the representative category is the category with the most posts for the place. A tie is resolved by the latest post.

Nearby and Radius Validation

  • lat and lng must be supplied together.
  • Latitude must be between -90 and 90.
  • Longitude must be between -180 and 180.
  • Radius must be a non-negative number.
  • Radius filtering is applied to both total count and returned rows.
  • sort=nearest requires coordinates.

This keeps list cards and map markers synchronized from the same filtered result set.

Modes

Accepted modes:

preview
expanded

Both modes use the same query rules. The client controls preview size and expanded pagination through page and limit.

Sorting

Implemented sorting:

  • nearest: shortest distance first.
  • most_posts: highest post count first.
  • most_popular: highest total views first.
  • recently_added: latest representative post first.
  • best_match: nearest then highest post count when coordinates exist; otherwise total posts then total views.

Stable location_group ordering is appended to prevent page-to-page ordering changes.

highest_rated is not accepted because the current database has no place-rating source.

Database View

Added:

migrations/20260807_update_views_place_list_categories.sql

The migration updates public.views_place_list with:

  • category_id.
  • category_name from categories.
  • latest_post.
  • A representative location_name, location_post, and thumbnail from the latest post per place and category.

The corrected view avoids grouping directly by location_post and thumbnail. This prevents one place from being split by individual post coordinates or images.

Existing filters remain:

p.is_publish = true
AND p.visibility = 'public'
AND p.banned = false
AND u.banned = false

Users pending deletion remain excluded.

Models

Updated PlaceListItem and PlaceListItemResponse with:

CategoryID   int64  `json:"category_id"`
CategoryName string `json:"category_name"`

PlaceListItem also includes internal LatestPost for query ordering.

Include Filtering

Selective responses support:

category_id
category_name

Existing selectable fields remain unchanged.

API Collection

Updated List Places.yml with:

  • Home Preview request using coordinates, radius, nearest sort, preview mode, and selected fields.
  • Home Expanded Category request using coordinates, category, search, radius, most-posts sort, and pagination.
  • Empty category result response example.

Tests

Added parameter tests covering:

  • Missing coordinate pair.
  • Latitude and longitude ranges.
  • Invalid mode.
  • Unsupported sort.
  • Default nearest sorting with coordinates.
  • Default best-match sorting without coordinates.

Files Changed

  • src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList.go
  • src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList_test.go
  • src/Models/PlacesModel.go
  • migrations/20260807_update_views_place_list_categories.sql
  • docs/migrations/views/DDL_views_place_list.sql
  • api-collection/Panorra API Feeds/Posts/Location/List Places.yml

Verification

Ran:

go test ./src/Action/V1/Places ./src/Models ./src/Controllers/V1 ./src/Routes/V1

Result: pass.

The database migration was applied separately. Verify deployed data with:

GET /places/list?lat=-6.5750346&lng=107.7902032&radius=25&mode=preview&sort=nearest&page=1&limit=3
GET /places/list?lat=-6.5750346&lng=107.7902032&radius=25&category_id=1&mode=expanded&sort=most_posts&page=1&limit=20

API: Support Panorra Mobile Home Places Near You + Category Filtering

Context

UI task GoThruMedia/panorra#2833 defines the new Panorra Mobile Home screen and expanded "Places Near You" bottom sheet. This API task covers the backend contract needed by that UI.

The current API repo already has:

  • GET /places/list
  • GET /categories

GET /places/list already supports nearby mode with lat, lng, radius, pagination, search, and selectable response fields. The Home UI now needs category-aware nearby place results that can power both the preview bottom sheet and expanded list.

Scope

Implement or extend API support for Home "Places Near You" so the mobile app can:

  • Load nearby places for the default Home preview.
  • Load expanded nearby place results after tapping "View all".
  • Filter places by category.
  • Return category data for Home filter chips.
  • Keep map markers and list results synchronized from the same query.
  • Support search, sort, pagination, and radius filtering for expanded state.

Proposed Endpoint

Prefer extending the existing endpoint:

GET /places/list

Add or confirm support for these query params:

lat=<float>
lng=<float>
radius=<km>
category_id=<int>
search=<string>
sort=best_match|nearest|highest_rated|most_popular|most_posts|recently_added
page=<int>
limit=<int>
include=<comma-separated-fields>
mode=preview|expanded

Category Requirements

  • GET /categories should return the category list needed by Home chips.
  • GET /places/list?category_id=<id> should return only places/posts matching that category.
  • Category filtering must work together with lat, lng, radius, search, sort, page, and limit.
  • If no category is selected, API should return the default Home category behavior, such as all nearby places.
  • Response should include category metadata where needed by the UI:
    • category_id
    • category_name
    • optional category slug/icon if available in the schema

Response Requirements

Each place item should support fields needed by the Home cards:

  • location_name
  • location_group
  • location_group_slug
  • location_post
  • thumbnail
  • distance_km
  • total_posts
  • total_views
  • contributors
  • contributors_overflow
  • category_id
  • category_name
  • save/bookmark state if supported for authenticated users

Acceptance Criteria

  • Mobile can request nearby Home preview places with category filtering.
  • Mobile can request expanded nearby places using the same filters.
  • category_id filters both list results and map marker results consistently.
  • Sorting works for at least nearest and most_posts.
  • Pagination does not return duplicate places.
  • Empty category results return a valid empty response, not an error.
  • Invalid category_id, lat, or lng returns a clear 400 response.
  • Existing clients using GET /places/list without category_id continue working.
  • API collection is updated with examples for default Home and expanded Home requests.

Related

  • UI task: GoThruMedia/panorra#2833
